**Derived columns (SP 800-53 rows only).** *Baselines* lists the SP 800-53 Rev 5 baselines (LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, PRIVACY) whose NIST resolved-profile catalogs include the control. *800-171r3 (derived via source 800-53 control)* lists SP 800-171 Rev 3 requirements whose NIST source-control references name exactly that control. CMMC Level 2 assessments reference SP 800-171 Rev 2, not Rev 3, so these derived Rev 3 links do not indicate CMMC alignment.

## MCP01: Token Mismanagement & Secret Exposure

Credentials that MCP servers need, such as API tokens and passwords, end up stored in plaintext config files, command-line arguments, logs, or model context where they can be read or leaked. Long-lived, over-scoped tokens make any exposure more damaging.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | IA-5(7) | Authenticator Management \| No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002 | A plaintext token in an MCP client config file's env, args, or headers is an unencrypted static authenticator kept in static storage, the condition this enhancement addresses. It does not cover leakage through logs or model context, so it is a subset of the need. | none | none |
| 800-53 | IA-5 | Authenticator Management | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002 | Tokens that MCP servers use to reach downstream APIs are authenticators whose content, strength, protection, and rotation fall under authenticator management. MCP-specific exposure paths such as tool output and model context are outside its focus. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.05.12 |
| 800-53 | SC-28 | Protection of Information at Rest | intersects_with | low | MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002 | MCP client config files store server credentials at rest on developer endpoints; protecting the confidentiality of that stored information addresses part of the secret-exposure need. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.08.05, 03.13.08 |
| 800-53 | AC-3 | Access Enforcement | intersects_with | low | - | Enforcing access authorizations on MCP config files and secret stores limits who and which local processes can read stored tokens; it reduces impact but does not remove the plaintext secret. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.02 |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.AA-01 | Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002 | Credentials issued to MCP servers are service credentials the organization must manage; tokens pasted into client config files are typically unmanaged, long-lived, and untracked. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.DS-01 | The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected | intersects_with | low | MCPXW-001, MCPXW-002 | Plaintext secrets in MCP config files are sensitive data at rest whose confidentiality must be protected; the subcategory also covers integrity and availability beyond this need. | - | - |

## MCP02: Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep

MCP servers are granted, or gradually accumulate, more access than their task needs, such as whole-disk filesystem access or broad API scopes. An agent misled into misusing a tool then acts with all of that excess privilege.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-006, MCPXW-010

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | AC-6 | Least Privilege | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-006, MCPXW-010 | An MCP server is a process acting on behalf of the user; whole-disk filesystem roots or privileged container options violate least privilege. Base AC-6 sets the principle but not ongoing review, which AC-6(7) adds. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.05 |
| 800-53 | CM-7(6) | Least Functionality \| Confined Environments with Limited Privileges | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-010 | MCP servers are user-installed software; running them in a confined container with limited privileges is this enhancement's aim, and flags such as --privileged or --pid=host defeat it. | none | none |
| 800-53 | AC-3 | Access Enforcement | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-006 | Access enforcement determines which files and resources an MCP tool can reach; a filesystem server rooted at / or the home directory enforces almost no boundary on what the agent may read or write. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.02 |
| 800-53 | CM-7 | Least Functionality | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-010 | Least functionality limits MCP servers to the capabilities their task requires and restricts risky functions such as host networking, host PID namespace, or Docker socket access for server containers. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.04.06 |
| 800-53 | AC-6(7) | Least Privilege \| Review of User Privileges | intersects_with | medium | - | MCP server entitlements such as filesystem roots, container flags, and API scopes tend to widen over time; periodically reviewing them and removing excess privilege is the direct counter to scope creep. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.05 |
| 800-53 | AC-6(1) | Least Privilege \| Authorize Access to Security Functions | intersects_with | low | MCPXW-006 | A filesystem MCP server scoped to the home directory can read security-relevant information such as SSH keys and cloud credentials; this enhancement restricts access to such information to authorized roles. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.05 |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.AA-05 | Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-006, MCPXW-010 | MCP server permissions (filesystem roots, container privileges, API scopes) are entitlements that should be defined, reviewed, and held to least privilege so scope does not creep over time. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-01 | Configuration management practices are established and applied | intersects_with | medium | - | Applying configuration management to MCP client config files gives a reviewed baseline for each server's granted scope, making privilege growth visible as a configuration change. | - | - |

## MCP03: Tool Poisoning

Tool names, descriptions, or schemas published by an MCP server carry hidden instructions or misleading content that steer the model into unintended actions. Because the model trusts tool metadata, a poisoned or later-altered definition can redirect behavior without the user noticing.

Scanner checks: none (not assessed statically; requires active analysis)

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | SI-7 | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | intersects_with | high | - | Integrity verification of the tool names, descriptions, and input schemas an MCP server returns from tools/list detects unauthorized changes to that information, including a silent rug-pull swap after approval. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SI-7(1) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Integrity Checks | intersects_with | medium | - | Checking a hash of each MCP server's tool definitions at session startup against an approved baseline is one concrete integrity check; it does not detect poisoning already present at approval time. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SI-10 | Information Input Validation | intersects_with | medium | - | Tool descriptions and schemas are inputs the MCP client passes to the model; validating them for hidden instructions, unusual characters, or out-of-place directives reduces poisoning. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SI-15 | Information Output Filtering | intersects_with | low | - | Where the organization operates the MCP server, validating that its tool names, descriptions, and schemas match expected content limits poisoning at the source; for third-party servers the client-side counterpart is SI-10. | none | none |
| 800-53 | CM-14 | Signed Components | intersects_with | low | - | Requiring signed MCP server packages establishes who published the tool definitions, but a signed server can still ship poisoned descriptions, so the overlap is indirect. | none | none |
| CSF 2.0 | ID.RA-09 | The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use | intersects_with | medium | - | Assessing an MCP server's integrity before use should include reviewing its tool descriptions and schemas, where poisoned instructions reside, not only the package that delivers them. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | DE.CM-09 | Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events | intersects_with | medium | - | Monitoring the MCP runtime environment for changed tool definitions and anomalous tool calls helps detect poisoning that was not caught at approval time. | - | - |

## MCP04: Software Supply Chain Attacks & Dependency Tampering

MCP servers are often fetched and run straight from public package registries or container images at launch time, frequently without a pinned version or integrity check. A compromised, typosquatted, or silently updated package then runs with the client's privileges.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-003, MCPXW-004

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | SI-7 | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-003 | Pinning MCP server packages to exact versions, and ideally image digests, is a precondition for verifying that the approved software runs; npx or docker launches of @latest allow no such check. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SR-4 | Provenance | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-003 | Recording which MCP server package, version, and registry each config launches maintains provenance; an unpinned stdio command resolves to whatever the registry serves at launch time. | none | none |
| 800-53 | CM-7(5) | Least Functionality \| Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-003, MCPXW-004 | Allow-by-exception for MCP servers means approving specific package versions; unpinned or auto-confirmed npx installs let unapproved code run on every client launch. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.04.08 |
| 800-53 | CM-11 | User-installed Software | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-004 | An MCP config that runs npx -y installs software at each launch without a user prompt; policy for user-installed software should govern and monitor such installs. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SR-3 | Supply Chain Controls and Processes | subset_of | medium | - | Supply chain controls and processes cover identifying and addressing weaknesses in the registries, maintainers, and build pipelines behind MCP server packages; the control is broader than this need. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.17.03 |
| 800-53 | SI-7(15) | Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity \| Code Authentication | intersects_with | medium | - | Cryptographically authenticating MCP server packages or container images before installation, for example by signature or digest, addresses tampering but not malicious code from a legitimate publisher. | HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SR-11 | Component Authenticity | intersects_with | low | - | Typosquatted or impersonating MCP server packages on public registries are a software analogue of counterfeit components; anti-counterfeit procedures apply only indirectly to open source packages. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | RA-5 | Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning | intersects_with | low | - | Scanning MCP server packages and their dependencies for known vulnerabilities finds some tampered or vulnerable components, but not novel malicious code inserted upstream. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.11.02 |
| CSF 2.0 | ID.RA-09 | The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-003, MCPXW-004 | Assessing an MCP server package's authenticity and integrity before use is defeated when the config fetches an unpinned version or auto-confirms installation at every launch. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | ID.AM-02 | Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-003 | An accurate software inventory needs exact MCP server versions; configs that launch @latest make the running version unknowable from the inventory. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | GV.SC-05 | Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties | intersects_with | low | - | Supply chain security requirements can be written into agreements with commercial MCP server vendors; most community MCP packages are used without any such agreement. | - | - |

## MCP05: Command Injection & Execution

An MCP server or its launch configuration passes untrusted input into shell commands, interpreters, or system calls, allowing arbitrary code to run on the host. Servers launched through a shell with inline scripts widen this exposure.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-005, MCPXW-010

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | SI-10 | Information Input Validation | intersects_with | high | - | MCP servers that forward tool arguments chosen by the model into shell commands or interpreters must validate those inputs; this is the core server-side mitigation for command injection. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | CM-7 | Least Functionality | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-005 | Launching an MCP server as a shell with an inline -c script gives the stdio command general-purpose execution capability; least functionality restricts launchers to the specific server binary. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.04.06 |
| 800-53 | CM-7(6) | Least Functionality \| Confined Environments with Limited Privileges | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-010 | Running MCP servers in confined environments with limited privileges contains the damage of a successful injection; privileged container launch flags remove that containment. | none | none |
| 800-53 | SC-39 | Process Isolation | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-010 | A separate execution domain for each MCP server process limits what injected commands can reach; container options such as --pid=host or --privileged break that isolation. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | AC-6 | Least Privilege | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-010 | Injected commands run with the MCP server's privileges, so least privilege for the server process and its container bounds the impact of command execution. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.05 |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-05 | Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-005 | Preventing execution of unauthorized software covers arbitrary scripts run through a shell-based MCP server launch or through injected commands. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-06 | Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle | intersects_with | medium | - | Secure development practices for MCP servers, such as avoiding shell invocation and validating tool arguments, prevent injection flaws at the source. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.IR-01 | Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage | intersects_with | low | MCPXW-010 | Protecting the host environment from unauthorized logical use limits what an MCP server compromised through command injection can reach, for example via host networking or the Docker socket. | - | - |

## MCP06: Prompt Injection via Contextual Payloads

Content returned by MCP tools or resources, such as web pages, files, or tickets, contains instructions that the model treats as commands. The agent's intended task is subverted and it may misuse other connected tools or leak data.

Scanner checks: none (not assessed statically; requires active analysis)

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | SI-10 | Information Input Validation | intersects_with | medium | - | Content returned by MCP tools and resources enters the model as input; validating or marking it as untrusted data reduces, but cannot fully prevent, instructions hidden in that content. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | AC-4 | Information Flow Enforcement | intersects_with | medium | - | Enforcing information flow policy between MCP servers, for example blocking data read by one tool from flowing into another tool's outbound call, limits what an injected instruction can accomplish. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.03 |
| 800-53 | AC-4(8) | Information Flow Enforcement \| Security and Privacy Policy Filters | intersects_with | low | - | Policy filters on MCP tool results, such as stripping or quarantining instruction-like content before it reaches the model, are one specific flow-control technique for this need. | none | none |
| 800-53 | SI-15 | Information Output Filtering | intersects_with | low | - | Where the organization operates the MCP server, validating that tool output matches the expected content type and shape catches some contextual payloads; for third-party servers the client-side counterpart is SI-10. | none | none |
| 800-53 | SI-4 | System Monitoring | intersects_with | medium | - | Monitoring MCP tool call sequences for attack indicators, such as an unexpected outbound request right after reading untrusted content, detects injection that preventive controls missed. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.14.06 |
| CSF 2.0 | DE.CM-09 | Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events | intersects_with | medium | - | Monitoring agent runtime behavior and the data flowing through MCP tools helps find adverse events caused by injected instructions. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.DS-10 | The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected | intersects_with | low | - | The model context is data in use; injected instructions can cause the agent to disclose or alter that data through other MCP tools. | - | - |

## MCP07: Insufficient Authentication & Authorization

MCP servers, especially remote ones, accept connections or tool calls without properly verifying who is calling or what they may do. Weak or missing authentication and cleartext transport let unauthorized parties invoke tools or intercept sessions.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-007, MCPXW-008, MCPXW-011

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | IA-9 | Service Identification and Authentication | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-007, MCPXW-011 | Remote MCP servers are services that clients connect to over HTTP or SSE; the client should authenticate the server (for example through TLS server identity) before tool calls are exchanged. | none | none |
| 800-53 | SC-8(1) | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity \| Cryptographic Protection | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-007, MCPXW-011 | A remote MCP transport over cleartext http:// exposes bearer tokens, tool arguments, and results in transit; TLS protects them but does not by itself authenticate or authorize callers. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.13.08 |
| 800-53 | IA-2 | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-008 | Organizational users invoking tools on a remote MCP server should be uniquely authenticated, for example through OAuth, so tool calls are tied to an accountable identity. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.05.01 |
| 800-53 | SC-23 | Session Authenticity | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-007, MCPXW-011 | MCP streamable HTTP and SSE transports rely on session identifiers; over cleartext these can be captured and replayed, so session authenticity protection applies. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.13.15 |
| 800-53 | AC-3 | Access Enforcement | intersects_with | medium | - | Authenticating the caller is not enough; the MCP server must also enforce which tools and resources each caller is authorized to use. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.02 |
| 800-53 | AC-17 | Remote Access | intersects_with | low | - | When an organization exposes an internal MCP server to remote clients, usage restrictions and authorization for that remote access apply; it does not cover third-party servers. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.12 |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.AA-03 | Users, services, and hardware are authenticated | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-008 | Users and services connecting to remote MCP servers, and the servers themselves, should be authenticated; a remote entry with no auth header is an item to verify against this outcome. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.DS-02 | The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-007, MCPXW-011 | Credentials, tool arguments, and results sent to a remote MCP server over plain HTTP are unprotected data in transit. | - | - |

## MCP08: Lack of Audit and Telemetry

Tool invocations, their arguments, and their results are not logged or monitored, so misuse by an agent or attacker goes unnoticed. Without records, incidents cannot be detected, investigated, or attributed.

Scanner checks: none (not assessed statically; requires active analysis)

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | AU-2 | Event Logging | intersects_with | high | - | Organizations must decide which MCP events are logged, such as server connections, tool invocations, arguments, results, and approval prompts; without that selection tool use leaves no trail. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, PRIVACY | 03.03.01 |
| 800-53 | AU-12 | Audit Record Generation | intersects_with | high | - | MCP clients, gateways, or servers need the capability to generate audit records for tool calls; many MCP deployments generate none by default. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.03.03 |
| 800-53 | AU-3 | Content of Audit Records | intersects_with | medium | - | Useful MCP audit records name the server, tool, arguments, outcome, time, and the user or agent on whose behalf the call was made. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.03.02 |
| 800-53 | AU-6 | Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting | intersects_with | medium | - | MCP tool call records only help if someone reviews them for inappropriate or unusual activity, such as an agent reading secrets then calling an outbound tool. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.03.05 |
| 800-53 | AU-10 | Non-repudiation | intersects_with | medium | - | Agents invoke MCP tools as processes acting on behalf of a user; without tamper-evident records binding each tool call to the user and agent session, the user can dispute having initiated it. Non-repudiation addresses that gap. | HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SI-4 | System Monitoring | intersects_with | medium | - | System monitoring of MCP traffic and tool activity provides detection where per-call audit logging is missing or incomplete. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.14.06 |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-04 | Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring | intersects_with | high | - | Log records of MCP tool calls should be generated and made available to continuous monitoring rather than left in client-local debug output. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | DE.CM-09 | Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events | intersects_with | medium | - | Monitoring MCP servers and agent runtimes for adverse events depends on telemetry from those runtimes being collected in the first place. | - | - |

## MCP09: Shadow MCP Servers

Users or teams add MCP servers to their clients without review or approval, outside the organization's inventory. These unvetted servers bypass security controls and are invisible to the people responsible for managing risk.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-009

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | CM-8 | System Component Inventory | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-009 | MCP servers configured in client config files are system components that belong in the component inventory; shadow servers are by definition missing from it. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | 03.04.10 |
| 800-53 | CM-8(3) | System Component Inventory \| Automated Unauthorized Component Detection | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-009 | Comparing discovered MCP client configs against an approved server allowlist is automated detection of unauthorized software components. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | CM-7(5) | Least Functionality \| Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-009 | A deny-all, permit-by-exception list of approved MCP servers, reviewed periodically, is the direct preventive control for unapproved servers. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.04.08 |
| 800-53 | CM-11 | User-installed Software | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-009 | Adding an MCP server to a client config is user-installed software; installation policy, enforcement, and compliance monitoring address shadow servers. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| 800-53 | SA-9 | External System Services | intersects_with | low | - | Remote MCP servers are external system services; requiring provider security commitments and oversight applies once the organization knows the server is in use. | LOW, MODERATE, HIGH, PRIVACY | 03.16.03 |
| CSF 2.0 | ID.AM-02 | Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained | intersects_with | high | MCPXW-009 | MCP servers are software and services that must be in the maintained inventory; the scanner's server inventory is evidence for building it. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.PS-05 | Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-009 | An MCP server launched from a config without approval is unauthorized software execution that this outcome aims to prevent. | - | - |

## MCP10: Context Injection & Over-Sharing

Sensitive data flows into the model's context or across tool and session boundaries more broadly than needed, where other tools, users, or prompts can reach it. Shared or persistent context turns one over-broad data source into an exposure path.

Scanner checks: MCPXW-006

| Framework | Control | Title | Relationship | Confidence | Checks | Rationale | Baselines | 800-171r3 (derived) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 800-53 | AC-4 | Information Flow Enforcement | intersects_with | medium | - | Controlling which data may flow from MCP tools into the shared model context, and from there into other tools, is information flow enforcement between connected components. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.03 |
| 800-53 | AC-6 | Least Privilege | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-006 | A filesystem MCP server scoped to / or the home directory can pull far more data into context than the task needs; least privilege limits what can be over-shared. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.01.05 |
| 800-53 | SC-4 | Information in Shared System Resources | intersects_with | low | - | By analogy, the model context and any persistent memory shared across MCP sessions, tools, or users act as a shared resource; SC-4 targets residual data in such resources, so the fit is indirect. | MODERATE, HIGH | 03.13.04 |
| 800-53 | AC-21 | Information Sharing | intersects_with | low | - | Before data reaches a third-party MCP server, users or automated mechanisms should confirm that the recipient is authorized for that data; this applies only to deliberate sharing decisions. | MODERATE, HIGH | none |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.DS-10 | The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected | intersects_with | medium | - | Data placed into the model context by MCP tools is data in use; protecting its confidentiality means limiting what enters context and who or what can read it back. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.AA-05 | Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties | intersects_with | medium | MCPXW-006 | Least-privilege entitlements for MCP servers, such as narrow filesystem roots, bound the data that can be over-shared into context. | - | - |
| CSF 2.0 | PR.DS-01 | The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected | intersects_with | low | MCPXW-006 | Data at rest on the endpoint becomes exposed when an over-broad MCP filesystem server can read it into the model context. | - | - |
